newsitem.title: UK: Med refiners turn to N. Sea as Urals price soars.
newsitem.headline: Med refiners turn to N. Sea as Urals price soars.

text.p: North Sea crudes are an increasingly attractive option for Mediterranean refiners as problems at the Black Sea port of Novorossiisk stoke up the price of Russian Urals, traders said.

"Urals is getting expensive," said an Italian refiner. "We are considering North Sea grades such as Oseberg and Forties. They're already interesting with Urals (moving towards) Dated minus 30 (cents)."
The last Urals cargoes were traded at a firm Dated Brent -37 and -38 cents.
"It's a combination of general maintenance at Novo plus bad weather," the refiner said.

Berth number one at Novorossiisk is to close for maintenance from December 9-24, while shipments of crude from the port were halted for 86 hours this morning due to pipeline and storage tank repairs, a port official said.

The berth slated for closure is the only one of the four loading berths at Novorossiisk which can load up to one million barrels. Its closure will cut exports by a 25-50 percent during the maintenance period, traders said.
Tight supplies of Urals is expected to push prices even higher in December and distillate-rich North Sea grades such as Forties, Oseberg and Brent will offer Med refiners better margins.
"Brent would be better for us than Urals. Brent gives 65 cents more than Urals. Sweet is definitely better than sour." said another Italian refiner.
A million barrels of Norwegian Oseberg have already moved south this month and more is expected to follow, supporting prices for some North Sea grades.
"More and more interest is coming from the Med," said a trader for a major North Sea producer.
But some Mediterranean refiners have already covered their December requirements with sour grades.
"We covered earlier when (Urals) prices were not so high. We don't really have the possibility to go for North sea grades," said a crude buyer for a Spanish refiner.
Med refiners said that North sea crude offered a better deal than gas oil-rich West African grades which are all but sold out for December.
"Forcados is too expensive (at Dated Brent +65 cents). It's not a good alternative," said one.
